May the LGII choose not to follow the afore-cited DBM Regional Opinion4 on what are "essential operating expenses" of the LGLI under the re-enacted budget and disburse funds following the MOOE appropriations in the 2013 budget already re-enacted in the current year per Section 232 of the LGC?" In your letter you alleged that despite the timely submission of the executive budget of the LGU for the current year, the Sangguniang Bayan (hereinafter referred to as "SB") failed to enact the 2014 budget ordinance of the LGU covering the General Fund, 20% Economic Development Fund (EDF), 5% Calamity Fund and 2% Discretionary Fund for the current year. For failure of the SB to pass the budget ordinance for the current year, your local government unit (LGU) is now on a re-enacted budget effective April 2014 following Section 323 of the Local Government Code (hereinafter, the "Code"), viz: "Section 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. [f the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and efgct until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is pgssed by the sanggunian concerned. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. In the implementation of such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concerned shall exclude from the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like national aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. " [Underscoring ours] Considering the limitations set forth in Section 323 of the Code, your LGUs implementation of development plans and the delivery of the essential and basic servhces to its constituents for the year is severely affected. Hence, this request. 1st and 2nd Queries The first sentence of Section 323 of the Code needs no further elucidation as it clearly states that if the SB fails to pass an ordinance authorizing the annual budget, it shah confinue to hold sessions, until such ordinance is approved and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. It is an elementary rule in statutory construction that when the words and phrases of a statute are clear and unequivocal, their meaning must be determined from the language employed and the statute must be taken to mean exactly what it says.5 The above-mentioned provision further provides that "if the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the appropriations is passed by the Sanggunian concerned" 6. Hence, by necessary implication, the SB can take up other matters after the lapse of the 90-day period considering that the LGU is already operating on a reenacted budget subject to certain limitations. Anent the possible liabilities of the concerned officials of the SB in the first instance, reference should be made to Section 60 of the Code to determine the applicable ground/s for disciplinary action. 3rd & 4th Queries: "Additional R mun rati n " an Di b ri n c Bu The matter being within the administrative expertise of the Department of Budget ana' Management (DBM), this Department deems it proper to refer the same for an authoritative interpretation of said agency. Under Section 323 of the Code only "statutory obligations, " or those demandable obligations derived from an express provision of law7, and "contractual obligations," or those obligations incurred by virtue of contracts entered into by the local chief executive pursuant to Section 2 (cy of the Coue, that were authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursements shall be in accordance therewith. Clearly, a continuing infrastructure development project of the LGU which was allegedly covered by a validly executed Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and authorized in the annual or supplemental budget of the preceding year is among those deemed reenacted. 7th Query; Continuing Appropriations Infrastructure projects already authorized in the preceding year's appropriations ordinance are classified as "continuing appropriations"9 and are available to support obligations incurred pursuant to the implementation of the infrastructure project even when these obligations are incurred beyond the budget year. By express provision of Section 32210, reversions of continuing appropriations shall not be allowed unless obligations therefor have been fully paid or otherwise settled. Clearly, following Section 322 in relation to Section 323 of the Code, appropriations for contractual obligations of LGUs, such as the infrastructure project funded from the 2096 economic development fund that were authorized in the budget of the preceding year as in this case, may be lawfully disbursed until the project is completed. Inc. vs. Hon. Altagra Court ratiocinated: Villaflor, etal (G.R. No. 128509. August 22, 2006), the Supreme "Discretion, " when applied to public functionaries, means a power or right conferred upon them by law or acting officially, under certain circumstances, uncontrolled by the judgment or conscience of others. A purely ministerial act or duty in contradiction to a discretional act is one which an officer or tribunal performs in a given state of facts, in a prescribed manner, in obedience to the mandate ofa legal authority, without regard to or the exercise of his own judgment upon the propriety or impropriety of the act done. Ifthe law imposes a duty upon a public officer and gives him the right to decide how or when the duty shall be performed, such duty is discretionary and not ministerial. The duty is ministerial only when the discharge Of the same requires neither the exercise ofofficial discretion or judgment. Notably, Republic Act No. 9485, otherwise known as the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007, excludes from its coverage those offices performing legislative functions, among others, as it covers offices exercising purely ministerial functions. 1 J Nonetheless, disciplinary action against erring members of the SB may be commenced based on the applicable ground/s as enumerated under Section 60 of the Code. BM In e re "Essential Operating Expenses " The interpretation of the DBM of "essential operating expenses" is persuasive and deserves respect under the "Doctrine of Respect for Administrative or Practical Construction" as explained by the Supreme Court 2nd Division in Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corpration vs. Philippine Gaming Jurisdiction Incorprated, et al. (G.R. IVO. ITR$$. April 2009), viz: "In applying said doctrine, courts often refer to several factors which may be regarded as bases thereof—factors leading the courts to give the principle controlling weight in particular instances, or as independent rules in themselves. These factors include the respect due the governmental agencies charged with administration, their competence, expertness, experience, and informed judgment and the fact that they frequently are the drafters of the law they interpret; that the agency is the one on which the legislature must rely to advise it as to the practical working out of the statute, and practical application of the statute prewnts the agency will' unique opportunity and experiences for discovering deficiencies, inaccuracies, or improvements in the statute. " " Section 114 RA 7160

In view of the foreg . g pronouncement of the Court, the interpretation/opinion of the DBM on the subject is controlling, hence, should be accorded weight and respect. Notwithstanding the foregoing opinion, the Municipality of Libmanan is not precluded from seeking the DBM of the DOJ's opinion should it find the foregoing opinion insufficient.
